main_body: Flat sand ground patch (4x3 tiles) with sparse speckles; terrain, not a standing object
top_band: none - uniform sand tone with scattered dots; no top/front structure (terrain tile)
evidence: The candidate is a flat ground texture. The column scan shows a uniform sand tone (L=182) with occasional 1-row darker or lighter speckle dots, so there is no standing volume and the 3/4 contract does not apply. It reads as a seamless terrain patch, which is correct for this kind.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 4 distinct colours and a median of 4 per tile, against 26 per tile and 80 colours for the grass reference, and 7 for paving. Sand base plus one lighter and one darker speckle gives only about 3 shading steps, against about 5-6 in Beodeul. The speckles are sparse and repeat in an obvious pattern across the tiles (the same dashes at rows 12, 28 and 44 and the same diagonals), so it looks mechanically tiled. Flat-fill coverage is 0% only because the dots break up the surface, but the ground is mostly one tone. It is far less rich than the grass reference and thinner than the paving reference, so it fails.
